The first lake is the largest, and the only one with a road along its shore. Its water is clear to a depth of several metres in late summer.

The second lake is shallow and warm, and reeds cover its northern end.

The third lake lies in a hollow between two ridges, and the path to it climbs for an hour through pine forest before it drops to the water. Few visitors make the walk, so the shore is quiet even in August, and the only sound is the wind in the pines.

The fourth lake is the smallest, and it freezes first each winter.
